title: Cohomological representability for a Grothendieck weak-Serre derived subcategory
statement: Fix one universe $U$ for the small sets, coproducts and Hom groups below [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal B$ be a Grothendieck abelian category relative to $U$ [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] and let $\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal B$ be a full replete subcategory containing zero, closed under kernels and cokernels of morphisms between its objects, and under extensions of its objects computed in $\mathcal B$. Suppose $\mathcal A$ is itself Grothendieck abelian with its induced exact structure and is closed under $U$-small coproducts in $\mathcal B$. In the ordinary unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], put $\mathcal Q=D_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal B)=\{K\in D(\mathcal B):H^q(K)\in\mathcal A\text{ for all }q\in\mathbf Z\}$. Then $\mathcal Q$ is a locally $U$-small triangulated full subcategory [def-weil-triangulated-category], closed under all $U$-small ambient coproducts, and those coproducts are represented by the termwise coproducts of complexes in $\mathcal B$. For every additive functor $H:\mathcal Q^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Ab}_U$ which carries distinguished triangles to long exact sequences and carries $U$-small coproducts to products, there are $R\in\mathcal Q$ and an isomorphism of functors $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal Q}(-,R)\cong H$.

source.place: Hall--Neeman--Rydh, arXiv:1405.1888v2, Appendix A, Theorem A.3, with the localizing-subcategory observation immediately after it, and Brown representability for well-generated triangulated categories (Neeman, Triangulated Categories, Theorem 8.3.3; see also the Brown application in HNR Lemma A.1). Archives WANTED; read HNR online. No Stacks tag supplies the well-generation assertion.

proof.text: Apply functorial K-injective existence to $\mathcal B$, then derived local smallness: $D(\mathcal B)$ has $U$-small Hom sets, as does its full subcategory $\mathcal Q$. The weak-Serre triangulated-subcategory lemma applies because all its zero, repleteness, kernel, cokernel and extension hypotheses are explicitly assumed. Thus $\mathcal Q$ is triangulated with the inherited structure.

source.place: Tag 06UQ, lemma-cohomology-in-serre-subcategory; injectives.tex, Tag 079P, theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck; derived local-smallness Hom computation preceding Tag 07D9

proof.text: The termwise-coproduct lemma gives ambient $U$-small derived coproducts. Coproducts in $\mathcal B$ are exact: express each as the filtered colimit over finite subsets of the index set of finite direct sums, and use exact filtered colimits in the Grothendieck definition. With the K-injective resolutions from step 1, cohomology therefore preserves these coproducts. Hence $H^q(\bigoplus_i K_i)\cong\bigoplus_iH^q(K_i)$ lies in $\mathcal A$ when all $K_i\in\mathcal Q$. Fullness restricts the ambient coproduct universal property to $\mathcal Q$, including the empty family.

source.place: Tag 07D9, lemma-derived-products, clauses (1)-(2); cohomology compatibility in lean/WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/DerivedCategory/HomologyCoproducts.lean

proof.text: The small-generators lemma applies to the given pair $(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)$: both categories are Grothendieck in $U$, the induced inclusion is exact by the assumed kernel/cokernel conditions, and it preserves $U$-small coproducts by the closure assumption and fullness. Obtain a $U$-small family $P$ with $\mathcal Q=\operatorname{Loc}_{D(\mathcal B)}(P)$.

source.place: Appendix A, Theorem A.3, its proof, and Lemma A.1

proof.text: Apply the set-generated-derived solution-set theorem to $D(\mathcal B)$, $P$ and $\mathcal Q$. Its minimality hypothesis is exactly step 3; the ambient Hom universe and the coproducts are those of steps 1-2. For the given cohomological, coproduct-to-product functor $H$, obtain a $U$-small family $(B_j,b_j)$ such that every $z\in H(Z)$ equals $H(f)(b_j)$ for some $f:Z\to B_j$.

source.place: Brown step: existing set-generated-derived solution-set theorem, specialized to the Hall--Neeman--Rydh generators

proof.text: Countable coproducts from step 2 split idempotents in $\mathcal Q$. Apply cohomological solution-set representability using this, local smallness and the family of step 4. It gives $R\in\mathcal Q$ and natural bijections $\alpha_Z:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal Q}(Z,R)\to H(Z)$ of underlying sets.

Put $r=\alpha_R(\mathrm{id}_R)$. Naturality for $f:Z\to R$ gives $\alpha_Z(f)=H(f)(r)$. Since $H$ is additive, $H(f+g)=H(f)+H(g)$ as homomorphisms $H(R)\to H(Z)$, so $\alpha_Z(f+g)=\alpha_Z(f)+\alpha_Z(g)$ and $\alpha_Z(0)=0$. Thus each bijection is an abelian-group isomorphism, and the already established naturality gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal Q}(-,R)\cong H$ as the asserted group-valued functors.

source.place: Elementary additive upgrade of the Brown representing bijections; explicit naturality calculation

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q13-e7165720e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, its 6 steps and the new node lem-sfb-weak-serre-derived-small-generators in full. Source: HNR arXiv:1405.1888 Appendix A, read online. Theorem A.3 says that if M ⊆ A is a weak Serre subcategory closed under coproducts and M is Grothendieck, then D_M(A) is well generated; Lemma A.1 and Remark A.2 cover localizing subcategories of D(A) with a set of generators. Its hypotheses match the item's and the new node's one for one, with no Serre condition added and no D(A)=D_A(B) identification. The new node's conclusion, Q = Loc_{D(B)}(P) for a small set P, follows from A.3, Lemma A.1 and the standard Brown/orthogonality argument. It asserts set generation only, not representability, so it does not restate the item, and the DAG search found no duplicate. Steps 1-2: K-injective existence, local smallness, the weak-Serre triangulated subcategory, termwise coproducts, and AB4 written out so that cohomology commutes with coproducts and A's coproduct closure applies; the empty family is included. Step 4: the hypotheses of set-generated-derived-solution-set are met exactly. Step 5: idempotent completeness from countable coproducts and solution-set representability. Step 6: the additive Yoneda upgrade is correct. Test cases A=B, A=0 and the empty coproduct work. I accept the 9 generic categorical tool_uses. No SGA source is used, and no fixes were needed.
